title: Verdier trace classes commute with restriction to an open subscheme of the support
statement:
Fix the coefficient conventions of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], $A=A_{E,n}$, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$. Let $X,C$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes, let $c=(c_1,c_2):C\to X\times_sX$ be an admissible correspondence with $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ and $u:Lc_2^*K\to Rc_1^!K$ as in [def-trf-correspondence], and let $j_W:W\hookrightarrow C$ be the inclusion of an open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion]. Put $c|_W=c\circ j_W=(c_1j_W,c_2j_W):W\to X\times_sX$ and let
$$
u|_W:L(c_2j_W)^*K\xrightarrow{\sim}Lj_W^*Lc_2^*K\xrightarrow{Lj_W^*u}Lj_W^*Rc_1^!K\xrightarrow{\sim}Rj_W^!Rc_1^!K\xrightarrow{\sim}R(c_1j_W)^!K,
$$
using the pullback composition isomorphism of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], the identification $Lj_W^*\cong Rj_W^!$ for the open immersion $j_W$ (clause (6) of [prop-functor-package], relative dimension $0$) and the composition isomorphism of [def-trf-admissibility]. Let $F=\operatorname{Fix}(c)$ with $i_F:F\to C$ as in [def-trf-fixed-scheme], and let $j':F_W=i_F^{-1}(W)\hookrightarrow F$ be the open subscheme over $W$; the fibre-product property identifies $F_W$ with $\operatorname{Fix}(c|_W)$. Then
$$
\operatorname{Tr}_{c|_W}(u|_W)=j'^*\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)\qquad\text{in }\operatorname{Hom}_{D(F_W,A)}(A_{F_W},\omega_{F_W,A}),
$$
where $\operatorname{Tr}$ is the Verdier trace class of [def-trf-trace-class] and, for a section $\sigma:A_F\to\omega_{F,A}$, $j'^*\sigma$ is the composite $A_{F_W}\simeq Lj'^*A_F\xrightarrow{Lj'^*\sigma}Lj'^*\omega_{F,A}\cong Rj'^!\omega_{F,A}\cong\omega_{F_W,A}$ built exactly as the restricted section of [def-trf-local-term] (open-immersion purity and [thm-trf-dualizing-complex-composition]). When $F_W$ is open and closed in $F$, this is the restricted section $j_{F_W}^*\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)$ of [def-trf-local-term].

source.place: §1.1.9 (restriction u|_W of a c-morphism to an open W of C), §1.2.2(a)-(b) (Tr is a morphism of complexes on C and Tr_beta is its restriction), and the first paragraph of the proof of Theorem 2.1.3 (Fix(c|_W)=Fix(c) on W; replacing C by C \ [Fix(c) \ beta] gives Tr_beta=Tr_c), with the two legs interchanged

proof.text: Write $j=j_W$, $i=i_F$, $i_W:F_W\to W$, $d:F\to X$ and $d_W=dj'$. A test-scheme map to $\operatorname{Fix}(cj)$ is a pair $(w:T\to W,x:T\to X)$ with $cjw=\Delta_Xx$, exactly a map to $W\times_CF$ by [def-trf-fixed-scheme]. Thus $F_W=\operatorname{Fix}(cj)$ scheme-theoretically, $ji_W=ij'$ and $ci=\Delta_Xd$. The two squares paste to the fixed square for $cj$.

Apply [lem-trf-open-fixed-square-domains] to $X,C,c,j$. It supplies separated finite-type domains and arrows for both fixed squares, including closed $i,i_W$ and open $j'$. The last paragraph of [def-trf-admissibility] supplies the constructible exceptional adjunctions for these maps. By [prop-functor-package], all the operations used below preserve their stated finite-stage domains, and open purity gives the normalized $Rj^!\simeq Lj^*$ and $Rj'^!\simeq Lj'^*$. We use $D^b_{ctf}(-,A)$ throughout.

source.place: §0.2; remaining domain argument of returned step 1

proof.text:
Put $H_c=\mathcal H_c(K)$, $H_{cj}=\mathcal H_{cj}(K)$ and let $\widetilde u,\widetilde u_W$ be the coefficient mates of [def-trf-trace-class-source]. Apply [lem-trf-open-hom-mate] with $M=Lc_2^*K$, $N=Rc_1^!K$, $f=u$. The composition identifications in the statement identify its $f_W$ with $u|_W$. It gives
$$E_j\widetilde u_W=Rj^!(\widetilde u)\,a,\qquad a:A_W\xrightarrow{\sim}Rj^!A_C.\tag{1}$$

source.place: §0.3(a)-(b), equation (0.3); first part of returned step 2

proof.text:
Put $Z=X\times_sX$ and $P=K\boxtimes_A^LD_XK$. Let $\xi_c:H_c\xrightarrow{\sim}Rc^!P$ and $\xi_{cj}:H_{cj}\xrightarrow{\sim}R(cj)^!P$ be the external-duality maps. Apply [lem-trf-external-duality-composition] to the same $c,K,j$. Under the canonical exceptional compositors it yields
$$\xi_{cj}=Rj^!\xi_c\circ E_j.\tag{2}$$
The helper fixes the canonical maps and the external product order; it introduces no symmetry sign.

source.place: §0.3, equations (0.3)-(0.4); second part of returned step 2

proof.text:
By [lem-trf-trace-map-from-external-duality], write
$$\varphi_c=Ri_*\gamma_d\circ\beta_c\circ Rc^!e_K\circ\xi_c:H_c\to Ri_*\omega_F,$$
and use the corresponding formula for $cj$. Here $e_K:P\to R\Delta_*\omega_X$ is the same map for both supports. Its arrow $Bc$ is clause (2) of [thm-trf-fixed-point-base-change]. That clause uses the conjugate specified by [def-trf-admissibility], read in the inverse direction, so $Bc$ is exactly the inverse-conjugate $\beta_c$ of [thm-sf-dual-base-change]; likewise for $cj$.

source.place: §1.2.2(a), displayed objectwise trace composite; identification retained from returned step 3

proof.text:
Apply the vertical-pasting clause of [thm-sf-dual-base-change] to the fixed square of $c$ ($f=c$, $g=\Delta_X$, $f'=d$, $g'=i$) stacked on the restriction square of step 1 ($f=j$, $g=i$, $f'=j'$, $g'=i_W$); by step 1 the pasted square is the fixed square of $cj$, and by step 2 all its schemes and arrows are separated of finite type. With $\beta_j:Rj^!Ri_*\xrightarrow{\sim}Ri_{W*}Rj'^!$ the inverse-conjugate exchange of the restriction square, the clause says that under the compositors $R(cj)^!\simeq Rj^!Rc^!$ and $R(dj')^!\simeq Rj'^!Rd^!$
$$\beta_{cj}=\beta_jRd^!\circ Rj^!\beta_c.$$
By naturality of the first compositor, $R(cj)^!e_K$ corresponds to $Rj^!Rc^!e_K$, so $\beta_{cj,\omega_X}\circ R(cj)^!e_K=\beta_{j,Rd^!\omega_X}\circ Rj^!(\beta_{c,\omega_X}\circ Rc^!e_K)$, with the same $e_K$ on both sides. Functoriality of dualizing composition in [thm-trf-dualizing-complex-composition] gives, under the exceptional compositors,
$$\gamma_{dj'}=\gamma_{j'}\circ Rj'^!\gamma_d.$$
Insert these equalities and (2) into the two trace composites of the previous step. Naturality of $\beta_j$ at $\gamma_d$ gives
$$\varphi_{cj}=Ri_{W*}\gamma_{j'}\circ\beta_{j,\omega_F}\circ Rj^!\varphi_c\circ E_j.\tag{5}$$
This is equality of maps $H_{cj}\to Ri_{W*}\omega_{F_W}$.

source.place: §1.2.2(a), second and third arrows; vertical pasting of dual base change (returned step 3)

proof.text:
Let $\sigma=\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)$ and $v=\varphi_c\widetilde u:A_C\to Ri_*\omega_F$. By [def-trf-trace-class] and the global-sections/direct-image compositor in [lem-trf-trace-map-from-external-duality], $\sigma$ is the ordinary $Li^*\dashv Ri_*$ adjunct of $v$. Indeed both global-sections adjunctions transpose the composite $\varphi_c\widetilde u$, and the displayed compositor identifies their composite with the $i$-adjunction. The same description holds for $cj$. Substituting (1) into (5) gives
$$\varphi_{cj}\widetilde u_W=Ri_{W*}\gamma_{j'}\circ\beta_{j,\omega_F}\circ Rj^!v\circ a.\tag{6}$$

source.place: §1.2.2(a); first paragraph and equation (6) of returned step 4

proof.text:
Apply [lem-trf-open-exchange-section-adjunct] to $i,j$, $S=\omega_F$, the section $\sigma$ and its adjunct $v$. Before the last $Ri_{W*}\gamma_{j'}$ in (6), its $i_W$-adjunct is $Lj'^*\sigma$ followed by open purity. Naturality of the ordinary adjunction with respect to $\gamma_{j'}$ therefore identifies the adjunct of (6) with
$$A_{F_W}\simeq Lj'^*A_F\xrightarrow{Lj'^*\sigma}Lj'^*\omega_F\simeq Rj'^!\omega_F\xrightarrow{\gamma_{j'}}\omega_{F_W}.$$
By the preceding step the adjunct on the left is $\operatorname{Tr}_{cj}(u|_W)$, while this displayed composite is exactly the statement's $j'^*\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)$.

If $F_W$ is also closed in $F$, the composite just obtained is the restricted section of [def-trf-local-term], since that definition uses the same constant-pullback, open-purity and dualizing-composition maps. This proves the last clause without an integration or properness requirement.
